newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, still stuck in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, still stuck in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Tuesday in another sluggish session, with front months buoyed slightly by a steady cash though prices remained in recent technical ranges, sources said.
July gained 1.2 cents to close at $2.159 per million British thermal units. August settled 1.3 cents higher at $2.17. Others ended mixed, with some 1998s losing ground.

"When we couldn't make a new high (early), the locals were dead set on stopping the uptrend, but the moving averages are close to crossing (up) and I think the next move will be higher," said one Texas-based trader, noting a stable cash.
While Gulf prices started the month below index, values since have held steady at lower levels without any weather support, the Texas trader said.
"I can't imagine a more bearish temperature scenario over the last few weeks, yet cash prices have held. At some point, there has to be heat," he said.
But not everyone agreed a rally was imminent, citing forecasts through the month for some heat in the South but no major weather in the critical Northeast and Midwest regions.

"For the next week or two, the forecast is for below-normal Northeast and Midwest weather, and with the July 4th weekend coming up and a lot of industrials set to shut down for a couple of weeks, my bias is lower," said one East Coast trader.
Chart watchers agreed recent ranges were intact, with July support still seen at $2.055 and $2 and resistance at $2.21, $2.25 and $2.37.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's AGA stock report range from 75 bcf to 110 bcf versus an 87 bcf gain last year.

In the cash Tuesday, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas held steady in the mid-to-high teens. Midcon pipes gained a couple of cents to about the $2.05 level. New York city gate gas was flat on the day in the low-to-mid $2.40s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip gained one-half cent to $2.236. NYMEX said 22,847 contracts traded, down from Monday's revised tally of 25,571.

On the KCBT, July finished one cent higher at $2.02, while deferreds ended mixed. The East/West spread widened by 0.2 cent to 13.9 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 227 lots traded, down from Monday's total of 387.
